newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed as payrolls data looms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed as payrolls data looms.

text.p: U.S. shares trading in London were mixed in thin volumes on Friday and dealers said the Dow looked set to open a few points lower although its fate was in the hands of key U.S. employment data due at 1330 GMT. "People have been waiting for these figures all week and they will set the tone for Wall Street," one dealer said. "We'll just have to wait to see if they contain any surprises."
Analysts polled by Reuters expect December nonfarm payrolls to be up 192,000 and December unemployment to be 5.3 percent.
By 1150 GMT, March S&P futures were down 1.90 points to 757.00 on Globex. March T-bonds were up 5/32 at 111-18/32.

"We have the most important number of the week coming up and that's going to determine how the market's going to go," another dealer said. "But at the moment the Dow looks like it will open marginally lower, maybe five to seven points."

Motorola was up $3/8 at $64-3/8 after releasing fourth-quarter earnings after the close on Thursday. "The figures looked better than expected but there's an analysts' meeting this morning so we'll see how that goes," a trader said.
Motor stocks were firm, with General Motors up $3/8 at $59-1/2 after the company settled a dispute with Volkswagen over alleged industrial esponage.
"They settled their industrial espionage dispute with Volkswagen, and although the terms were much less than some expected at least it's out of the way," a dealer said.
He said reports that General Motors was exploring a public offering of its stake in Delphi Automotive Systems, the world's largest automotive parts supplier, were also helping the stock.
Ford was up $1/4 at $34 after reports it was planning a partial sale of its car rental business Hertz, traders said.
They said some technoloy stocks were weaker with the chip industry's December book-to-bill ratio largely ignored despite indicating higher sales.
Intel was down $1/4 at $142-3/4, Texas Instruments fell $1/8 to $66-1/4 and IBM was $3/8 down at $161-5/8. "IBM saw some profit-taking," a dealer said.
